title: Haboush symmetric-power lifting for a trivial quotient representation
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $H$ a reductive group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] over $k$. Here reductive means smooth, affine and of finite type with geometrically connected fibres and with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure; unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation every geometric point is a unipotent matrix. A rational $H$-module is a $k$-vector space $V$ with a $k$-linear coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_k k[H]$ satisfying $(\rho_V\otimes1)\rho_V=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho_V$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho_V=1_V$, where $\Delta,\epsilon$ are the comultiplication and counit of the coordinate Hopf algebra; $V^H=\{v:\rho_V(v)=v\otimes1\}$. If $V$ is finite-dimensional and $\lambda:V\twoheadrightarrow k$ is a surjective equivariant linear map to the trivial module, there are $N>0$ and $q\in(\operatorname{Sym}^N_kV)^H$ with $\operatorname{Sym}^N(\lambda)(q)=1$ under $\operatorname{Sym}^N_k k\simeq k$. Here $\operatorname{Sym}^N_kV$ is the degree-$N$ component of the commutative algebra freely generated by $V$, with its induced coaction. No assumption on the characteristic or on algebraic closedness of $k$ is made.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5 and Lemma 9.2.5 (5-prime), equivalently Lemma 9.2.8 (1),(2),(6): finite-dimensional symmetric-power form of Haboush. Read online arXiv:1005.2398v3, printed pp.43--45,49--50; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Put $V_K=K\otimes_kV$ and $W=\operatorname{Hom}_K(V_K,K)$ with contragredient action $(g\ell)(v)=\ell(g^{-1}v)$ after every scalar extension. The surjection $\lambda$ gives a nonzero fixed vector $x=\lambda_K\in W$: equivariance says $\lambda_K(g^{-1}v)=\lambda_K(v)$. The group $H_K$ is reductive by the geometric condition in the hypothesis. A basis of $V$ identifies $\operatorname{Sym}^n_K V_K$ with $K\otimes_k\operatorname{Sym}^n_kV$ by sending each degree-$n$ basis monomial to the same monomial; this identification respects the induced coactions and $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)$. The argument below first constructs a degree-$n$ invariant over $K$ and then descends it.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 dual formulation (5-double-prime) and Remark 9.2.7; agent-written field-extension and dualization details.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-simply-connected-cover] over the algebraically closed field $K$ to $H_K$. Obtain $p:T\times S\to H_K$ with $T=\mathbf G_m^r$ and $S$ semisimple simply connected. Pull the rational action on $W$ back along $p$. In particular $x$ remains fixed. The injectivity of $p^*:K[H_K]\to K[T\times S]$ will allow invariance for this product group to imply invariance for $H_K$.

source.place: Proposition 21.60 and Remark 18.27; field version of the reductions preceding the determinant argument in Alper Theorem 9.7.5.

proof.text: Write the torus coaction in the Laurent-monomial basis of $K[T]=K[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$: $\rho_T(w)=\sum_{a\in\mathbf Z^r}w_a\otimes z^a$, with finite support. Coassociativity gives $\rho_T(w_a)=w_a\otimes z^a$, and the counit gives $w=\sum_aw_a$. Uniqueness of Laurent coefficients makes this a direct sum $W=\bigoplus_aW_a$. Let $U=W_0$ and $\pi:W\to U$ be the coefficient projection. Since $S$ commutes with $T$, its coaction preserves each $W_a$: apply its coaction to the displayed identity and compare Laurent coefficients. Thus $U$ is a rational $S$-module and $\pi$ is $S$-equivariant and $T$-invariant, where $T$ acts trivially on $U$. Also $x\in U$ and $\pi(x)=x$. This coefficient computation includes $r=0$ and works in arbitrary characteristic.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, printed pp.234--235: explicit coassociativity proof of the weight decomposition, with the commuting-action projection written out.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-steinberg-endomorphism-detection] to the finite-dimensional rational $S$-module $U$ and its nonzero fixed vector $x$. Obtain $E
e0$ and $\varphi:U	o\operatorname{End}_K(E)$ with $\varphi(x)
e0$ and $\operatorname{End}_K(E)^S=K\operatorname{id}_E$. Equivariance makes $\varphi(x)$ invariant, hence $\varphi(x)=c\operatorname{id}_E$ for some $c
e0$. Replacing $\varphi$ by $c^{-1}\varphi$ gives $\varphi(x)=\operatorname{id}_E$. Set $n=\dim_K E>0$.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5 proof, normalization of the endomorphism-valued map using Lemmas 9.7.2 and 9.7.4; field specialization.

proof.text:
Choose a basis of $E$ and let $a_{ij}\in U^*$ be the entries of the linear map $\varphi$. Form the actual element
$$f=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{j=1}^n a_{\sigma(j),j}\ \in\operatorname{Sym}^n_K(U^*).$$
This is the determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], so $f(x)=\det(\varphi(x))=1$. The square case $m=n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] has just one subset in its sum, and gives $\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B)$ over every commutative ring. Apply this over the polynomial algebra in the coordinates of $U$, tensored with $K[S]$, to the universal action matrix $B$ on $E$. Equivariance gives $\varphi(su)=B\varphi(u)B^{-1}$, whence
$$\det(B\varphi(u)B^{-1})=\det(B)\det(\varphi(u))\det(B^{-1})=\det(\varphi(u)).$$
Here $\det(B)\det(B^{-1})=\det(I)=1$. This identity in the coordinate algebra, rather than just at rational points, is exactly $\rho(f)=f\otimes1$ for the induced polynomial coaction. Thus $f$ is an invariant homogeneous polynomial of positive degree.

source.place: Theorem 9.7.5 final determinant construction; multiplicativity from Stacks Tag 0F0K, algebra-item-cauchy-binet.

proof.text: Pull $f$ back by $\pi$: $F=\operatorname{Sym}^n(\pi^*)(f)\in\operatorname{Sym}^n(W^*)$. It is fixed by $S$ because $\pi$ is equivariant and fixed by $T$ because $\pi$ is $T$-invariant. For every commutative $K$-algebra $A$ and $(t,s)\in(T\times S)(A)$, the product action gives $(t,s)\cdot F=t\cdot(s\cdot F)=t\cdot F=F$. Apply this also to the universal pair over $K[T\times S]$ to obtain the product coaction identity. If $d=\rho_{H_K}(F)-F\otimes1$, then $(1\otimes p^*)(d)=0$. The map $1\otimes p^*$ is injective: expand in a vector-space basis of $\operatorname{Sym}^n(W^*)$ and use the injectivity of $p^*$ on each coefficient. Hence $d=0$. The canonical linear map $V_K\to W^*$ sends $v$ to $(\ell\mapsto\ell(v))$. On a basis and its dual basis it is an isomorphism; the formula $(g\ell)(v)=\ell(g^{-1}v)$ shows it is equivariant. Its symmetric power therefore identifies $F$ with $q_K\in(\operatorname{Sym}^n V_K)^{H_K}$. Evaluation at $x=\lambda_K$ sends each generator $v$ to $\lambda_K(v)$, so it is exactly $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda_K)$. Consequently $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda_K)(q_K)=F(x)=f(\pi(x))=1$.

source.place: Remark 9.2.7 and Theorem 9.7.5; explicit product-group descent and double-dual polynomial identification (agent-written).

proof.text:
Finally use the degree-$n$ monomial basis from Step 1. The finitely many $K$-coefficients of $q_K$ and $1$ span a finite-dimensional $k$-subspace of $K$. Since $1\ne0$, extend $\{1\}$ to a basis $1=b_0,b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of this subspace and write $q_K=\sum_{j=0}^t b_j\otimes q_j$, with $q_j\in\operatorname{Sym}^n_k V$. Its invariance is
$$\sum_{j=0}^t b_j\otimes(\rho(q_j)-q_j\otimes1)=0.$$
Linear independence of the $b_j$ gives $\rho(q_j)=q_j\otimes1$ for every $j$ (extend them to a $k$-basis of $K$ and take coordinate projections). Likewise $\sum_jb_j\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q_j)=1=b_0$ gives $\operatorname{Sym}^n(\lambda)(q_0)=1$. Taking $N=n$ and $q=q_0$ proves the assertion over $k$. No averaging or division by $n!$, and no invariance assumption only on $H(k)$, has been used.

Step 5: f = det(a_ij) uses the signed formula; invariance is a coaction identity in K[U-coordinates] tensor K[S], from Cauchy-Binet with m=n and det(B)det(B^-1) = det(I) = 1; there is no division, so p dividing n is fine. lean.statement: theorem exists_invariant_symmetric_power_lift {k : Type u} [Field k] (H : Scheme.{u}) [H.Over (Spec (.of k))] [GrpObj (H.asOver (Spec (.of k)))] [IsAffine H] (hH : ReductiveTorusCentralizer.IsReductive (Grp.mk (H.asOver (Spec (.of k))))) (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] (ρ : V →ₗ[k] V ⊗[k] Γ(H, ⊤)) (hcoassoc : HopfAction.Coassociative k Γ(H, ⊤) V ρ) (hcounit : HopfAction.Counital k Γ(H, ⊤) V ρ) (ell : V →ₗ[k] k) (hell : Function.Surjective ell) (heq : ∀ v : V, ell.rTensor Γ(H, ⊤) (ρ v) = ell v ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : Γ(H, ⊤))) : ∃ (N : ℕ) (q : SymmetricAlgebra k V), 0 < N ∧ q ∈ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι k V).range ^ N ∧ SymmetricAlgebra.lift ((SymmetricAlgebra.ι k V).rTensor Γ(H, ⊤) ∘ₗ ρ) q = q ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : Γ(H, ⊤)) ∧ SymmetricAlgebra.lift ell q = 1
lean.note: The degree-N element is represented in the full symmetric algebra with membership in the Nth power of the generator range. SymmetricAlgebra.lift extends the original coaction on generators, and lift ell is the canonical degree-N evaluation to k. Separate field and vector-space universes. The explicit affine instance is already a consequence of hH and exposes the canonical coordinate Hopf structure; it adds no restriction.
